Record date: 2129-01-15
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 01/15/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of renal function, and mental health reassessment.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax presents for follow-up approximately five weeks after his last visit. He reports that his respiratory symptoms have not significantly improved. He continues to experience marked exertional dyspnea, particularly when engaging in activities such as climbing stairs or walking briskly. His usage of the albuterol inhaler remains frequent, averaging six times daily. The productive cough persists with clear sputum, and he denies any hemoptysis or recent respiratory infections.
Mr. Fairfax expresses ongoing concern regarding the bilateral lower extremity edema, which seems to have worsened. Despite adhering to a sodium-restricted diet and continuing furosemide at 200 mg daily, he reports no substantial reduction in swelling. He has gained 2 pounds since the last visit, indicating persistent fluid retention. He rates the discomfort from the edema as 7/10.
His mental health concerns have escalated; he reports increased anxiety levels, particularly surrounding his health and the implications of his physical limitations. Sleep disturbances persist, with difficulty falling asleep and frequent awakenings. He has continued attending cognitive-behavioral therapy sessions but expresses a desire for additional psychiatric support.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + exertional dyspnea, + productive cough, + wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - + increased anxiety, + insomnia, no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using six times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 200 mg daily (no change). 7. Sertraline 150 mg daily (no change). 8. Prednisone 40 mg daily for COPD exacerbation (completed course).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.7F, HR 78, BP 135/82, RR 24, O2 sat 84% on room air.
General: Elderly male in moderate respiratory distress, appears fatigued but cooperative. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 9.2, Hgb 10.5, Hct 31.0, Plt 210. 2. BMP: Na 134, K 4.6, Cl 101, CO2 22, BUN 45, Cr 2.8, Glucose 90. 3. BNP: 700 (elevated). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 2.5 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's respiratory status shows no significant improvement. Given the persistent symptoms and increased reliance on bronchodilators, a referral to pulmonary medicine for further evaluation and potential adjustment of his COPD management plan is warranted. Consideration for a nebulized bronchodilator may be appropriate. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. The serum creatinine has worsened, indicating further renal impairment. Nephrology will be consulted urgently for assessment and management of his renal function. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema remains significant despite diuretic therapy. Reinforce dietary sodium restrictions and continue furosemide at 200 mg daily. Daily weight monitoring remains essential, and nephrology follow-up will be pursued. 4. Mental health: Mr. Fairfax will continue with sertraline at 150 mg daily. A referral to psychiatry for medication management will be expedited due to increased anxiety and insomnia. Continued engagement in cognitive-behavioral therapy is encouraged.
Patient education reiterated regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
